answer.summary: Revolut gives product teams substantial autonomy to move quickly and build many products, while founders retain broad visibility and step in through reviews and detailed scrutiny to ensure quality and sound decisions—not to micromanage every step.

sections.heading: Autonomy with accountability
sections.content: Zlokazov says the ideal product owner is fully autonomous and can keep building even if metrics are not yet there, provided they can explain the reasoning behind their decisions and roadmap when challenged. Teams present weekly product outputs to founders, who provide steering and use reviews as a last line of control to check that the work makes sense and is thoroughly considered.

sections.heading: Leadership oversight without routine micromanagement
sections.content: Founders have an overview of everything, and every shipped screen is reviewed by them. But they do not need to be involved in every detail of execution: they go deep on areas that matter most or need scrutiny, and intervene when necessary. Zlokazov describes this balance as enabling more products to ship, faster; he also cites small, autonomous teams building credit products for 50 countries as an example of the approach’s scale.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately describes autonomous teams shipping many products without routine micromanagement, balanced by founders’ visibility, reviews, challenges, and intervention when needed. These points are supported by the cited transcript excerpts.
